title: Inquest into death of machete-carrying man begins on Monday
article: An inquest into the death of Darrell Elroy Barnes, shot dead by police after being confronted for carrying a machete, will begin Monday morning.
Owen Court of the B.C. Coroners Service will preside over the inquest, which is slated to run until Aug. 3 in Burnaby.

On the evening of July 22, 2011, police spotted the 48-year-old man carrying a machete near Powell and Dunlevy streets in the Downtown Eastside. After confronting Barnes, the officers initially used a beanbag shotgun in an attempt to disarm the man before turning to their firearms.
Barnes was transported to hospital but pronounced dead shortly after.
The RCMP's homicide team was brought in to investigate at the request of Vancouver police and it was announced in December that an inquest would also take place.

Along with a jury, court will hear evidence from witnesses to determine details of Barnes's death. While the inquest does not assign blame or responsibility in the death, it is a chance for court to make recommendations in preventing similar deaths in the future.
